newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia Henkel unit 1996 sales up 3 pct.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia Henkel unit 1996 sales up 3 pct.

text.p: Slovenian cosmetics producer Henkel-Zlatorog, a subsidiary of Germany's Henkel KGaA, said on Monday 1996 revenue rose 3.2 percent to 9.6 billion tolars ($62.2 million).
Henkel-Zlatorog is 51-percent owned by Henkel, while 49 percent of the company is in the hands of Slovenian trading company Zlatorog.
The company said the improved revenue was due to increased exports. Last year Henkel-Zlatorog exported 44 percent of its production, up from 41 percent a year before.
The firm said 1996 profit was "satisfactory" but declined to reveal exact figures.

"We expect revenue and profit will remain unchanged in 1997 as growth is unlikely due to tough competition in Europe," chief executive Andrej Mesaric told Reuters. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
